transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because I'm having some trouble keeping things straight lately. 

I just... I can't seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. There's a lot going on right now—patent notes and team decisions for work, and then other things like workshop prep and gallery deadlines... I don't know. It's just getting messy. I end up starting whatever is loudest at the moment, instead of focusing on what actually matters. 

So... yeah. I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Has this difficulty staying organized and focused been a lifelong pattern for you, or is it something that started more recently?

Um... I suppose it's not really a new thing. Looking back... I think it was there in grade school, too. 

My teachers used to write that I was bright, but... that I daydreamed. A lot. I'd lose my homework folders, or... I'd actually finish an assignment and just forget to hand it in. 

So... yeah. It goes back to long before I was a teenager.
Do you find yourself struggling with persistent, excessive worry about everyday matters?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I stress about missing deadlines, but... I don't think I worry excessively about everyday things. Just the usual stuff, I guess.
Over the past few weeks or months, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, downheartedness, or hopelessness?
No, not really. I mean... I get frustrated with myself sometimes when things pile up, but... I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. Just... overwhelmed, I guess.
